questions.question: The least common multiple of 12, 18 and 27 is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Numbers: 12, 18, 27

**Calculation:**

Prime factorization:

12 = 2² × 3

18 = 2 × 3²

27 = 33

To find the LCM, use the highest powers of all primes:

LCM = 2² × 3³

LCM = 4 × 27

LCM = 108

**The least common multiple (LCM) of 12, 18, and 27 is 108.**

questions.question: A vehicle is going at one-fourth of its usual speed and it takes an extra 45 minutes to reach its destination. Its usual time to cover the same distance is:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

New speed = 1/4 of usual speed

Extra time = 45 minutes = 0.75 hours

**Formula Used:**

Time = Distance / Speed

**Calculation:**

Since new speed is 1/4 of the usual, it takes 4 times longer to cover the same distance.

Let usual time = T hours

New time = 4T

Extra time taken = New time - usual time

⇒ 0.75 = 4T - T

⇒ 3T = 0.75

⇒ T = 0.75/3

⇒ T = 0.25 hours

**Usual time to cover the distance = 0.25 hours or 15 minutes**

questions.question: The average weight of 49 students is 53 kg. When a new student is admitted to the class, the average decreases by 500 g. Find the weight of the new student.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

The average weight of 49 students = 53 kg

When a new student is admitted (now 50 students), the average decreases by 500 g = 0.5 kg

New average = 53 kg - 0.5 kg = 52.5 kg

**Formula used:**

Total weight = Average weight × Number of students

**Calculation:**

Total weight of 49 students = 53 × 49

Total weight with 50 students = 52.5 × 50

Weight of the new student = Total weight with 50 students - Total weight of 49 students

⇒ 53 × 49 = 2597 kg

⇒ 52.5 × 50 = 2625 kg

**Weight of the new student = 2625 kg - 2597 kg = 28 kg**

questions.question: A sum of money amounts to Rs. 1,200 in 2 years and becomes Rs. 1,260 in 3 years at compound interest, when interest is compounded annually. What is the rate of compound interest per annum?
questions.solution:
Given:

 
• The amount after 2 years is Rs. 1,200.
 
• The amount after 3 years is Rs. 1,260.

Let P be the principal amount and r be the annual interest rate.

From the compound interest formula:

The amount A after t years is given by:

 A = P (1 + r)t

Using the given information:

 
• After 2 years: 1200 = P (1 + r)2
 
• After 3 years: 1260 = P (1 + r)3

To find r , divide the second equation by the first equation to eliminate P :

( (1260)/(1200) = (P (1 + r)³)/(P (1 + r)²) )

( (1260)/(1200) = 1 + r )

 

⇒1 + r = 1260/1200

⇒ 1 + r = 1.05 

⇒ r = 0.05 

So, the rate of compound interest per annum is:

⇒ r = 0.05 × 100% = 5 %

Therefore, the rate of compound interest per annum is 5 %

questions.question:
Two mixtures A and B have the following compositions:

Mixture A has copper and tin in a ratio of 1 ∶ 2

Mixture B has copper and tin in a ratio of 1 ∶ 3

If equal quantities of mixtures A and B are used for producing mixture C, then find the ratio of copper and tin in mixture C.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Mixture A: Copper : Tin = 1:2

Mixture B: Copper : Tin = 1:3

**Calculation:**

Let's assume equal quantities mean taking 1 unit of each mixture.

For Mixture A (1 unit):

Total parts = 1 (Copper) + 2 (Tin) = 3 parts

Copper in A = 1/3 of mixture A

Tin in A = 2/3 of mixture A

For Mixture B (1 unit):

Total parts = 1 (Copper) + 3 (Tin) = 4 parts

Copper in B = 1/4 of mixture B

Tin in B = 3/4 of mixture B

For Mixture C (combining 1 unit of A and 1 unit of B):

Copper in C = Copper in A + Copper in B = (1/3 of A + 1/4 of B) = 1/3 of 1 + 1/4 of 1 = 1/3 + 1/4 = (4 + 3)/12 = 7/12 units

Tin in C = Tin in A + Tin in B = (2/3 of A + 3/4 of B) = 2/3 of 1 + 3/4 of 1 = 2/3 + 3/4 = (8 + 9)/12 = 17/12 units

Copper : Tin in C = 7/12 :(17)/12 = 7 : 12

**Thus, the ratio of Copper to Tin in Mixture C is 7:17.**

questions.question: If the HCF of 45 and 55 is expressible in the form of 55 × 5 + 45m, then what is the value of m?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

HCF of 45 and 55

**Calculation:**

HCF = 55 × 5 + 45m

Now, HCF(45, 55) = 5

Substitute the values:

⇒ 5 = 55 × 5 + 45m

⇒ 5 = 275 + 45m

⇒ 45m = 5 - 275

⇒ 45m = -270

⇒ m = -270/45

⇒ m = -6

**Therefore, the value of m is -6.**

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, 30% of the electorate did not cast their votes. 20% of the votes polled were found invalid. The winning candidate got 64% of the valid votes and won by a majority of 3136 votes. Find the number of voters enrolled in the voter list.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

30% did not vote, so 70% of (V) voted.

20% of the votes polled were invalid, so 80% of the votes polled are valid.

The winning candidate got 64% of the valid votes.

The winning candidate won by a majority of 3136 votes.

**Calculation:**

⇒ Votes Polled ((VP)) = 70% of (100x) = (70x).

⇒ Valid Votes ((VV)) = 80% of (70x) = (0.8 × 0.7x = 56x).

⇒ The winning candidate got 64% of (VV), and the losing candidate got 36% of (VV) (since 100% - 64% = 36%).

The difference between the votes for the winning and losing candidates is 64% - 36% = 28% of (VV).

Given that this difference is 3136 votes,

⇒ [0.28 × 56x = 3136]

⇒x = 3136/(0.28 × 56)

⇒ x = 20000

**Therefore, the number of voters enrolled in the voter list is 20,000.**

questions.question: Determine the LCM of two numbers if their HCF is 12 and their ratio is 13 ∶ 15.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

HCF (Highest Common Factor) = 12 Ratio of two numbers = 13 : 15

**Formula used:**

LCM = (Number1 × Number2) / HCF

**Calculation:**

Let the two numbers be 13x and 15x, where "x" is a common multiple, and in this case, it is equal to the HCF.

Therefore, the two numbers are 1312 and 1512 (since HCF = 12).

⇒ Number 1 = 13 × 12 = 156 Number 2 = 15 × 12 = 180

LCM (Least Common Multiple) of two numbers is given by the product of the numbers divided by their HCF.

LCM = (Number1 × Number2) / HCF

⇒ LCM = (156 × 180) / 12

⇒ LCM = 28080 / 12 = 2340

**So, the LCM of the two numbers is 2340.**

questions.question: Kanchan lent Rs. 10,000 for 2 years and Rs, 5,000 for 4 years at the same rate of simple interest. If the total interest received by Kanchan is Rs. 2,000, then what was the rate of interest?
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Principal 1 (P1) = Rs. 10,000, Time 1 (T1) = 2 years

Principal 2 (P2) = Rs. 5,000, Time 2 (T2) = 4 years

Total Simple Interest (SI) = Rs. 2,000

Formula Used:

Simple Interest: SI = PR/T 100, where

P is the principal amount, R is the rate of interest, T is the time in years.

**Calculation:**

Total interest received is the sum of the interests from both principals: [SIₜₒₜₐₗ = SI₁ + SI₂]

[SI₁ = (P1 times R times T1)/(100)]+ [SI₂ = (P2 times R times T2)/(100)]

⇒[2000 = (10000 times R times 2)/(100) + (5000 times R times 4)/(100)] 

⇒ 2000 = 200R + 200R

⇒ 400R = 2000

⇒ [R = (2000)/(400) = 5]

**The rate of interest is 5% annually.**

**Therefore, the radius of the circle is 2.1 cm.**

questions.question: Find the mean proportion of x³y and xy³.
questions.solution:
__Shortcut Trick__

**Mean Proportion** between **a** and **b** is √(a × b).

Given values: **a = x³y** and **b = xy³**.

Mean Proportion = √(x³y × xy³) = √(x⁴y⁴) = **x²y²**.

**∴ The correct answer is x²y².**

**__Alternate Method__**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/61356aee096894ad366dfec0a4437de6e3354fcea923a8b88035ca9a40fbdd04.png] 

**Given:** First term (a) = **x³y**, Last term (b) = **xy³**.

**Formula Used:** If **M** is the mean proportion, then **a/M = M/b** ⇒ **M² = ab**.

⇒ M² = (x³y) × (xy³)

⇒ M² = x⁽³⁺¹⁾ × y⁽¹⁺³⁾

⇒ M² = x⁴y⁴

⇒ M = √(x⁴y⁴)

⇒ M = (x⁴)¹/² × (y⁴)¹/²

⇒ M = x²y²

**∴ The correct answer is x²y².**

**__Additional Information__**

Third Proportion

The **Third Proportion** of two numbers **a** and **b** is defined as **c** such that **a : b = b : c**, which gives **c = b²/a**.

Fourth Proportion

The **Fourth Proportion** of three numbers **a, b,** and **c** is **d** such that **a : b = c : d**, which gives **d = (b × c)/a**.

Compound Ratio

For two ratios **a : b** and **c : d**, the **Compound Ratio** is **(a × c) : (b × d)**.</p

questions.question: 36 equally efficient workers can paint 25 identical walls in 48 days. In how many days can 45 such workers paint 60 such walls?
questions.solution:
Given:

36 equally efficient workers can paint 25 identical walls = 48 days

Concept used:

M1D1/W1 = M2D2/W2

Calculations:

M1D1/W1 = M2D2/W2

⇒ (36 × 48)/25 = (45 × D)/60

⇒ D = (36 × 48 × 60)/(25 × 45)

⇒ D = 92.16

∴ Time taken to paint 60 walls by 45 workers is 92.16 days.

questions.question: Which of the following numbers leaves the remainder equal to the highest common factor of 6, 8 and 9, when divided by 6, 8 and 9?
questions.solution:
Given:

The number which when divided by 6, 8 and 9 leaves a remainder equal to the highest common factor of 6, 8 and 9.

Concept Used:

For the least number take LCM and also check that all conditions are satisfying or not

For same remainder in each case add the remainder in the LCM 

Calculation:

First we have to find the HCF of 6, 8, and 9.

HCF of 6, 8, 9

6 = 21 × 31 

8 = 23 

9 = 32 

HCF of 6, 8, 9 = 1

Now,

LCM of 6, 8, 9

6 = 21 × 31 

8 = 23 

9 = 32 

LCM of 6, 8, 9​ = 23 × 32 = 72

Check by options:

(i) 506 ÷ 72 = rem(2) ≠ 1

(ii) 575 ÷ 72 = rem(71) ≠ 1

(iii) 291 ÷ 72 = rem(3) ≠ 1

(iv) 433 ÷ 72 = rem(1) = 1

∴ 433 leaves the remainder equal to the highest common factor of 6, 8 and 9, when divided by 6, 8 and 9.

questions.question: The diameter of a hemisphere is equal to the diagonal of a rectangle of length 4 cm and breadth 3 cm. Find the total surface area (in cm²) of the hemisphere.
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Length (l) = 4 cm

Breadth (b) = 3 cm

Diameter of hemisphere = Diagonal of rectangle

**Formula:**

Diagonal of rectangle = √(l² + b²)

Radius (r) of hemisphere = Diameter / 2

Total Surface Area of hemisphere = 3πr²

**Calculation:**

Diagonal = √(4² + 3²) = √(16 + 9) = √(25) = 5 cm

Diameter of hemisphere = 5 cm

Radius (r) = 5 / 2

Total Surface Area = 3π × (5/2)² = 3 × π × 25/4 = (75pi )/(4) cm²

**∴ Option 2 is the correct answer.**

questions.question: Jimmy has to cover a distance of 88 Km in 16 hours. If she covers half of the journey in (3)/(4) time, then what should be her speed to cover the remaining distance in the time left?

Speed = Distance/Time

questions.question: The cost price of pulses is 12% less than the selling price. Using a faulty weighing machine, shopkeeper is able to earn 25% profit. How much per cent of the faulty machine shows more weight as compared to the actual weight (Rounded off to the nearest integer)?
questions.solution:
[IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/ca81259519cadfb2d5350673c220e419e60378e9770ad26512fc8e826a8d93f1.png] __Shortcut Trick__

Let the Selling Price (SP) per unit be 100, which means Cost Price (CP) per unit = 100 − 12 = 88.

The shopkeeper's overall profit multiplier is 125 / 100 (since he earns a 25% profit).

Overall Gain Factor = Price Factor × Weight Factor

125 / 100 = (100 / 88) × (Wₛₕₒwₙ / Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ)

Wₛₕₒwₙ / Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ = (125 / 100) × (88 / 100) = 110 / 100 = 11 / 10

The machine shows 11 units for every 10 units of actual weight, showing 1 extra unit per 10 units. Percentage extra = (1 / 10) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/c76c13ba2d2ab46b47f8a931ae621dac081a0cb266b142dc23f58659fac4a466.png] **__Alternate Method__**

**Given:**

Cost Price (CP) is 12% less than the Selling Price (SP).

Overall profit earned by the shopkeeper = 25%.

**Formula Used:**

Overall SP / Overall CP = (SP per unit / CP per unit) × (Shown Weight / Actual Weight)

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/3232e9a3b580247fe02e25959a0746e2ad0513c94158edb226547daed89afccf.png] 

**Calculations:**

⇒ Let the Selling Price per unit be ₹100.

⇒ Cost Price per unit = ₹100 − 12% = ₹88.

⇒ Let the machine display Wₛₕₒwₙ units of weight, while the actual physical weight dispensed is Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ units.

⇒ Overall CP incurred by the shopkeeper = 88 × Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ

⇒ Overall SP charged from the customer = 100 × Wₛₕₒwₙ

⇒ Since the overall profit is 25%, we know that Overall SP = Overall CP × 1.25

⇒ 100 × Wₛₕₒwₙ = 88 × Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ × (125 / 100)

⇒ 100 × Wₛₕₒwₙ = 88 × Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ × (5 / 4)

⇒ 100 × Wₛₕₒwₙ = 110 × Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ

⇒ Wₛₕₒwₙ / Wₐ꜀ₜᵤₐₗ = 110 / 100 = 11 / 10

⇒ This means for every 10 units of actual weight, the machine falsely shows 11 units.

⇒ Extra weight shown by the faulty machine = 11 − 10 = 1 unit.

⇒ Percentage more weight shown = (Extra Weight / Actual Weight) × 100

⇒ Percentage more weight shown = (1 / 10) × 100 = 10%.

**∴ The correct answer is 10%.**

 [IMAGE: https://cdn.repeatermock.com/tb/f13e2ad6582c16aa62a83672e2547ad20a01fddb61962a1acce42eb9a1a99caa.png] **__Additional Information__**

Dishonest Dealer Concept

When a dealer manipulates both price and weight, the effective profit multiplier is determined by the product of the price multiplier (SP ÷ CP) and the weight multiplier (Weight Charged ÷ Actual Weight Given).

Profit and Loss Basics

Profit is fundamentally evaluated on the base of the Cost Price (CP). The foundational formula is Profit% = [(SP − CP) ÷ CP] × 100.

Successive Multipliers

For multiple distinct profit sources, the overall change can be established rapidly using multiplying factors. For instance, a 25% profit strictly translates to a multiplier factor of (100 + 25) / 100 = 125 / 100 or 5 / 4.

questions.question: Two pipes can fill a cistern in 12 hours and 16 hours, respectively. The pipes are opened simultaneously and it is found that due to leakage at the bottom, it takes 90 minutes more to fill the cistern. How much time will the leakage take to empty the completely filled tank?
questions.solution:
Given:

Time is taken by pipe A to fill tank = 12 hours

Time is taken by pipe B to fill tank = 16 hours

Formula used:

Time = Total work/efficiency

Calculation:

Here, extra 90 minutes represents the extra time taken by the pipes due to the leak.

Total units of water to be filled = LCM of (12, 16) = 48 units.

Pipe A can fill 4 units of water in 1 hr.

Pipe B can fill 3 units of water in 1 hr.

Normal time taken to fill the tank = 48/7 hrs = 6(6/7) hrs.

With 90 min extra, the pipes would take (48/7 + 3/2) hr to fill the tank.

Let the leakage can empty N units of water in 1 hr.

⇒ (4 + 3 - N) × (48/7 + 3/2) = 48

⇒ (7 - N) × 117/14 = 48

 ⇒117N = 819 - 672

⇒ N = 147/117

Leakage can empty 1 units of water in 117/147 hr.

Leakage can empty 48 units of water in 117/147 × 48 = 5616/147

⇒ 1872/49 = 38 (10)/(49) hr

∴ Time taken to empty the tank is 38 (10)/(49) hrs.

questions.question: In an election between two candidates, the difference between the candidates who won and lost was 2,500 votes. The candidate who won got 75% of the votes, and there were no invalid votes. The total number of votes polled of the losing candidate was:
questions.solution:
**Given:**

Difference in votes = 2,500

Winning candidate got 75% of the votes

**Calculation:**

Let the total number of votes be (V).

Since there are only two candidates and no invalid votes, if the winning candidate got 75% of the votes, the losing candidate got 25% of the votes.

⇒ The difference in votes (75% - 25% = 50% of total votes) = 2,500.

So, (50% × V = 2,500).

⇒ (V = (2,500)/(0.5) = 5,000).

⇒ Votes for the losing candidate = 25% of total votes = (0.25 × V = 0.25 × 5,000 = 1,250).

**Total number of votes polled for the losing candidate = 1,250.**

questions.question: Sanjay and Rohan can complete a work in 8 days and 12 days, respectively. Starting with Sanjay, they work on alternate days. In how many days will the work be completed?

1 unit work done by Rohan in 1/2 days.
